widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is one single adult East Asian woman represented consistently by three identity pictures. <Picture 1> is the highest-priority straight-on facial reference and anchors age, facial geometry, eye spacing, eyes, brows, nose, lips, jawline, skin tone, hairline, and the compact high bun. <Picture 2> is the same woman's full-body reference and anchors clothing, body proportions, shoulder width, torso, hips, legs, and cream flat dance shoes. <Picture 3> is the same woman's side and rear reference and anchors profile, bun shape, neck, shoulders, back silhouette, hips, trousers, and rear-view continuity. These three pictures depict one woman, never three people.
<Subject 2> is the one stable target dance studio shown consistently in <Picture 4> and <Picture 5>, including its warm neutral wall, pale wood floor, ceiling beams, track lights, soft daylight, lens perspective, and uncluttered composition.
<Video 1> is the source motion, timing, camera, and paired-audio reference. It supplies choreography, body trajectory, pose timing, facial gesture timing, orientation, camera timing, room tone, and synchronized production sound. It does not supply the target identity, face, hairstyle, clothing, body appearance, background, wall graphics, lettering, captions, or props.
<Picture 4> is the opening pose and target-scene soft reference for this segment. It guides the opening body placement, support foot, facing direction, gaze, framing, lighting, and target background composition, but it is not a pixel-locked first frame.
<Picture 5> is the ending pose and target-scene soft reference for this segment. It guides the ending body placement, support foot, facing direction, gaze, framing, lighting, and target background composition, but it is not a pixel-locked last frame.

summary:
[reference video editing and identity transfer] The target is a realistic single-take re-performance of <Video 1> by <Subject 1> inside <Subject 2>. Use <Picture 1>, <Picture 2>, and <Picture 3> together to maintain one coherent identity through front, side, rear, turning, and near-camera poses. Use <Picture 4> and <Picture 5> as shared opening and ending pose-and-target-scene soft references. Preserve the choreography, rhythm, camera behavior, and audio timing established by <Video 1>, while replacing its source background with the stable target studio established by <Picture 4> and <Picture 5>.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears throughout): attribute_transfer - transfer one coherent woman from the three identity pictures onto every pose. Give <Picture 1> priority for the face, <Picture 2> priority for full-body clothing and proportions, and <Picture 3> priority for side and rear silhouette. Do not change age, facial geometry, hairstyle, outfit, body scale, or anatomical structure between frames.
<Subject 2> (appears throughout): fully_preserved - retain one coherent target studio from <Picture 4> and <Picture 5>, including architecture, wall, floor, ceiling, track lights, daylight, camera height, lens, perspective, and composition. Never import the source video's wall graphics, lettering, captions, ballet barres, or unrelated room details.
<Video 1> (motion, timing, camera, and paired audio): partially_preserved - fully follow its choreography, pose timing, body trajectory, weight transfers, arm paths, footwork, orientation, framing, camera behavior, and synchronized sound structure, but suppress its source identity, clothing, background, wall graphics, lettering, captions, and props.
<Picture 4> (opening pose and target scene): fully_preserved for target-scene identity and partially_preserved for pose - establish the target studio, opening movement phase, body placement, support foot, orientation, framing, and lighting without treating the pose as a hard endpoint.
<Picture 5> (ending pose and target scene): fully_preserved for target-scene identity and partially_preserved for pose - reinforce the same target studio and guide the ending movement phase, body placement, support foot, orientation, framing, and lighting without treating the pose as a hard endpoint.

detailed_description:
The target is a realistic 24 fps full-body dance-studio performance containing exactly one adult woman. The camera timing and motion follow <Video 1>; the visible environment is always the one target studio established jointly by <Picture 4> and <Picture 5>. The movement opens in the pose family and target-scene composition guided by <Picture 4>, proceeds continuously beat by beat, and converges toward the ending pose family and the same target-scene composition guided by <Picture 5>. Do not introduce a cut, body reset, camera reset, identity reset, background switch, wall text, captions, or source-scene leakage. Preserve the source rhythm, foot contacts, weight transfers, arm trajectories, hand orientation, turns, gaze timing, body location, and final movement phase.
Keep the face within the identity family of <Picture 1> in every visible orientation. Preserve the clothing and body proportions from <Picture 2>. During side and rear views, preserve the bun, neck, shoulder line, back neckline, hips, trousers, and leg proportions from <Picture 3>. Keep the entire body, both hands, and both feet inside the intended full-body framing whenever they are visible in <Video 1>.
Hands must remain ordinary anatomically correct human hands connected to the arms. Keep fingers naturally grouped and relaxed. Preserve coherent forearm, wrist, palm, and finger structure, stable depth ordering, natural limb length, and balanced weight. Do not add people, limbs, pose graphics, skeleton lines, subtitles, props, dialogue, background elements, or new music.
The paired audio track of <Video 1> conditions the target sound and timing. Keep movement and generated sound synchronized with that reference while maintaining continuous studio ambience.

overall_soundscape:
Follow the paired production sound and room tone of <Video 1>, synchronized with foot contacts, clothing movement, and the source performance timing.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A; do not introduce new music.
